content:
A few months ago, the MacBook Neo made a stunning debut, becoming the best-value laptop of 2026. Even with the recent price increase, it remains the most recommended entry-level laptop for most people. Much like other value offerings from Apple, this one also comes in several playful colourways, such as citrus, blush, indigo, and silver, giving the MacBook a distinct personality and burst of colour. But one complaint I've always had is that most MacBook accessories only come in shades to match the traditional silver or space grey. That's when Satechi stepped in with three brand-new accessories in matching colours.

I had actually reviewed the "larger" version of this product before, and I really liked it. It's the most versatile accessory in Satechi's new lineup. It expands one of your USB-C ports into five additional ports, and the form factor is excellent. It's roughly the size of a puck, and it has built-in MagSafe functionality. So you can use it with both your MacBook Neo and your iPhone at the same time. This USB-C hub offers the following:

  • HDMI output supporting 4K 60Hz video
  • USB-C pass-through charging up to 60W
  • USB-C port with transfer speeds up to 5Gbps
  • USB-A port with transfer speeds up to 5Gbps
  • Full-size SD card reader
  • A premium braided nylon USB-C cable

Thanks to the MagSafe functionality, the manufacturer includes an adhesive magnetic ring that can be stuck onto the lid of your MacBook Neo. And the metal portion of the magnetic ring is even colour-matched to the Neo! So even when you're not using the adapter, the ring doesn't look out of place. As I mentioned, this is my favourite of the three products because it's so versatile. It's compact, solidly built, has all the main ports most people need, and works with a wide range of devices.

The OntheGo Multiport Adapter comes in the same colours as the MacBook Neo and is available today on Amazon and the Satechi website, priced at $44.99.

This is the more familiar, traditional USB-C hub form factor. It clips onto the side of the MacBook Neo (hence the name "Snap Hub"), expanding it with 6 new ports, one more than the OntheGo hub above. The way it attaches firmly and seamlessly to the MacBook Neo makes it clear that it was designed specifically for the MacBook Neo. The Snap Hub offers the following:

  • SD and MicroSD card readers
  • USB-C pass-through charging up to 45W (enough to charge the MacBook Neo, since the Neo only supports up to 30W)

The Snap Hub is undoubtedly the most seamlessly integrated accessory of the three. It both looks and feels like an Apple-made product. It uses a two-tone design, with the top perfectly matching the material and colour of the Neo, but the rest of the exterior cleverly uses this soft-touch rubber material, because they know this part will sit against the Neo's metal exterior, and metal-on-metal friction generally doesn't work well. I think this is an excellent design choice. One thing to note is that this hub will occupy both of the Neo's USB-C ports, but the hub itself still provides two USB-C ports as well as additional...

The USB-C Snap Hub is available starting today in the four Neo colours mentioned above, also priced at $44.99, on Amazon and the Satechi website.

As the grand finale of Satechi's new Neo lineup, they've redesigned the Slim EX mouse to match the rest of the family. I had tested the non-coloured version of this mouse before, and it's one of the top recommendations purely on value for money. For $29, you get:

  • Connect up to 3 devices simultaneously — two via Bluetooth and one via the 2.4GHz receiver (the receiver is USB-C!)
  • Aluminium body
  • Charges via USB-C
  • User-replaceable battery
  • Up to three months of continuous use, and over a year in standby mode
  • Comes with a USB-C cable included for charging and connectivity

The build quality and finish of this mouse are on par with mice costing twice as much. It has a sleek, understated aluminium body that's ergonomic even during extended use. The ability to quickly switch between devices is a feature I use constantly, bouncing between my MacBook and iPad. Also, the fact that the 2.4GHz receiver uses USB-C instead of USB-A is a seriously underrated upgrade. While the Neo's trackpad is already excellent, I personally like to use the trackpad and mouse together. I use the trackpad for gestures and horizontal scrolling, and the mouse for finer...

The Slim EX wireless mouse is available in the four colours mentioned above, as well as the previously released black version. The mouse is priced at $29.99 and is available on Amazon and the Satechi website. If you want to save a bit of money, the black version is the exact same mouse and is currently on sale for just $23.99.

Conclusion

Satechi is the first manufacturer to launch this kind of colour-matched accessories for the MacBook Neo, and they seem to really understand their target audience. They offer high-quality, practical accessories for a MacBook Neo lineup that had to make compromises on pricing to hit that $699 mark. All of these accessories are solidly built and offer rich, practical functionality that enhances the MacBook Neo experience.

If I had to pick a favourite from the three, I'd lean slightly towards the OntheGo Multiport Adapter, purely because of its versatility and the fact that it works with any device that has a USB-C port and MagSafe. But the Snap Hub is just as excellent, with incredibly seamless physical integration with the Neo, and the Slim EX mouse is the cherry on top. What do you think? Are these accessories worth picking up? How important is colour-matching to you? Drop a comment and let's discuss!
